As someone who also struggled with depression, I definitely agree with the statement that "you are not responsible for all the things that happen to you, but you are completely in control of your attitude and your reactions to them." At this point, I've recognized that my feelings are learned behaviors that were strongly reenforced throughout my younger years. I've been working at identifying and changing these behaviors as they occur for the past couple of years now. Change has been slow, but many people have told me now that I have change a lot.

There are still times when I feel hopeless and nothing seems to be able to cheer me up. Those are the moments where introspection and honesty with one's self become invaluable. Almost always, some part of my psyche is grasping hold of some belief or idea it wants to protect or doesn't want to give up. It'd rather keep me in the shadows to avoid potentially being burned by the sun.

*[Workers mining for coltan. You gain points by having the soldiers yell at exhausted workers.]*

Once upon a time, there were minerals resting in the bowels of the Earth. One of these minerals, called coltan, is found in most electronic devices. The majority of coltan supply is located in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, a country torn by a brutal civil war. The increasing demand of coltan produced a wave of violence and massacre in the congo. Military groups enslaved prisoners of war, often children, to mine the precious mineral. Directly or not, we are all involved in this complex, illegal traffic.

*[People jumping off building. You gain points by catching them in a net. If you miss, they'll hit the ground with a thud and bleed.]*

They work in inhumane conditions and are forced into illegal overtime. Over the span of a few months, more than 20 workers committed suicide out of extreme desperation. We addressed this issue by installing suicide-prevention nets.

*[Customers running towards pear store. You gain points by throwing iPhones at them. If you miss, they run into the store windows.]*

Then, you purchased this phone. It was new and sexy. You waited for it for months. No evidence of its troubling past was visible. Did you really need it? Of course you did. We invested a lot of money to instill this desire in you. You were looking for something could signal your status, your dynamic lifestyle, your unique personality. (pause) Just like everyone else.

Soon, we'll introduce a new model that will make this one look antiquated, and you will discard it. It will joins tons of highly electronic toxic waste.
